intro_html: Picadinho is what a Brazilian kitchen makes when it wants beef stew without waiting all afternoon. The beef gets diced small instead of cubed large, which means more browned surface, faster cooking, and a piece of meat in every single spoonful. Carrots and sweet potato round it out. Each bowl carries 44 grams of protein and 566 calories for about $4.49.
cost_closing_html: About $4.49 a bowl. Dicing the beef small is not just a texture choice, it is a budget choice, because a small dice makes a modest amount of meat read as a lot more on the plate.
shop_smart: Dice the chuck yourself rather than buying pre cut stew meat. Pre cut costs more per pound and it is usually trim from cuts you would not have chosen.
Sweet potatoes carry a lot of the volume in this pot. They store for weeks in a cool dark spot, so buy the bag when the price is right.
Tomato paste comes in a small can and you use a couple spoonfuls. Freeze the rest in tablespoon blobs on wax paper and drop them straight into the next braise.
Cilantro goes in at the very end. Buy one bunch, use the stems in the pot and the leaves on top, and nothing goes in the trash.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chuck roast into a small dice, about half inch cubes, and pat it dry. Wet beef will not brown.
Sear the beef in the olive oil in batches over high heat, giving each batch room. Pull it out as it browns.
Cook the chopped onion and garlic in the same pot until soft, scraping up the browned bits.
Stir in the tomato paste and the cumin and cook a minute so the paste darkens.
Return the beef with the beef broth, cover, and simmer 60 to 75 minutes until the beef is tender.
Add the diced carrots and sweet potatoes and simmer uncovered another 20 to 25 minutes, until they are soft and the stew has thickened.
Turn off the heat, stir in the red wine vinegar and the chopped cilantro, then taste for salt and pepper.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot, subtract the empty-pot number you wrote down, and divide by 14. Spoon that weight into each of 14 containers, stirring the pot between scoops so the beef and the vegetables stay evenly split. Each bowl lands at 566 calories with 44 grams of protein.

steps: Cut the chuck roast into a small dice and sear it in batches in olive oil.
Soften onion and garlic in the pot, then cook in the tomato paste and cumin.
Return the beef with broth and simmer covered 60 to 75 minutes.
Add carrots and sweet potatoes and simmer uncovered until tender.
Finish with red wine vinegar and cilantro and portion into 14 containers.
